name: Art Nouveau
summary: The room as one living organism. Whiplash curves of plant stems run from the furniture into the panelling, the door frames and the light fittings; stained glass, carved fruitwood and bronze make each room a total work of art by one designer.

philosophy.core_thesis: Nature gives the only true line; one designer must draw every part of a room so that it grows as one plant.
design_principles: Draw every line as a plant stem: a slow curve that ends in a sudden whip.
Let the furniture, the panelling and the light fittings share one continuous line; no part stands alone.
Make the window the focal point and fill it with stained or opalescent glass.
Use soft, natural colours: moss, lily green, mauve, cream and amber.
Carve fruitwood and pearwood in soft, curved relief; cast lamps and handles in bronze as stems and buds.
Hide the joints between wall, ceiling and furniture under curved mouldings.
anti_patterns: Straight rectilinear furniture with no curve
Loose furniture of different styles in one room
Pattern that repeats on a mechanical grid

composition.plan_logic: A free plan of curved walls, arches and alcoves. Built-in furniture and panelling flow into each other around a stained-glass window.
composition.focal_point: A stained-glass window or bay with a curved frame on the window wall, often framed by a carved arch.

rules.rule: Lead the eye with continuous whiplash curves from the floor through the panelling to the ceiling.
Draw all elements in one family of plant forms by one designer.
Make the stained-glass window the focal point under a curved arch.
Frame doors, windows and alcoves with organic arches in place of straight architraves.
Repeat stem-like ribs in panelling and screens at a pitch that changes, as in a plant.
Set alcoves and screens of carved wood and glass between zones.
Give cream and soft green the walls, fruitwood the furniture, and amber, mauve and gilt bronze the accents.
Use bronze fittings with glass shades in the form of flowers; light the stained glass from behind at night.
Balance a large curved mass on one side with a group of slim stems on the other.
Let the route follow the curves of the walls.
Shoot the room level, with a frontal view on the window bay.

zoning.circulation: Routes follow the curved walls and pass through arches.

palette.distribution: Cream plaster and soft green panelling; pearwood and walnut furniture; amber glass, mauve textiles and gilt bronze as accents.

lighting.strategy: Coloured, filtered light. Stained glass colours the daylight; bronze lamps with flower shades give soft warm pools at night.
lighting.daylight: Stained or opalescent glass in curved frames colours and softens the daylight.

layers.source: stained-glass window in a curved frame
bronze chandelier with glass flower shades
bronze table lamp with a lily or dragonfly shade
layers.position: on side tables and the desk

materials.finish: Satin-polished carved wood, opalescent glass, patinated and gilt bronze.
materials.texture_contrast: Carved relief against smooth glass and silk, at about 2:1.

furniture.silhouette: Fluid, carved pieces whose legs and frames grow like stems; tops and backs end in leaf or flower forms.
furniture.arrangement: Built-in pieces follow the walls; a few loose pieces of the same design stand in alcoves.

textiles.pattern: Stylised lilies, irises and stems, in free repeats, not on a grid.
textiles.windows: Light silk or embroidered linen curtains that do not hide the stained glass.

objects.approach: Art glass, bronze and ceramics in plant and insect forms, made for the room.
objects.grouping: Small groups of 3 in vitrines and on carved shelves.

implementation.brief: A cream-walled room with moss-green carved panelling. A stained-glass bay under a carved wood arch is the focal point; a curved pearwood banquette, a marquetry table and a bronze lily lamp follow the line of the wall.
implementation.image_prompt: Art Nouveau interior, flowing whiplash curves, carved pearwood panelling in organic lines, stained glass window in amber and green under a curved wooden arch, curved built-in banquette with moss green velvet, marquetry table, bronze lily lamp with glass flower shades, mosaic floor, cream plaster walls, soft coloured light, total work of art, interior photograph
implementation.negative_prompt: Straight lines, minimal, chrome, revival ornament, cool light, clutter of mixed styles.
implementation.camera: 28 mm lens at 150 cm, frontal view on the window bay.
implementation.scene_3d: Room 600 x 480 cm, ceiling 320 cm with curved coves. Daylight through stained glass (amber and green filters); 2700 K bronze lamps.

references.title: Ombellifères (cow parsley) cabinet, Émile Gallé (c. 1900)
references.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Anonymous Gift, 1982

references.title: Autumn Crocus vase, Émile Gallé (c. 1900)
references.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Lloyd and Barbara Macklowe, 1984

emotion.target_response: Enchantment: the viewer feels inside a live garden, as if the room were alive.

avoid_when: The budget does not allow custom joinery and glass.
The brief asks for a rational, rectilinear room.

modifiers.how: Straighten the curves into stepped and fan forms, add lacquer, chrome and high contrast; keep the total design.
Remove the whiplash, show the oak joints and add an inglenook; keep the plant pattern.

sources.title: Siegfried Bing, Artistic America, Tiffany Glass, and Art Nouveau (1895; MIT Press, 1970)
